current.text: He re-signed with the Thunder on a 3-year, 75 million dollar contract.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle injury.
He missed many games with injuries last season. Early last season, while Chet Holmgren was out, he played at a top 40 level.
OKC's center rotation is Hartenstein, Chet Holmgren and Jaylin Williams. Jaylin Williams barely played unless one of the centers was out.
Experts expect him to be a full-time starter with a secure role. A teammate's strong preseason does not change that.
If he stays healthy and plays 28 to 29 minutes, experts see him as a top 60 player.
One expert gives a best case of 40th and a worst case of 93rd.
Lloyd ranks him 104 in Yahoo categories. Other experts say he should go inside the top 100, keep going too late, and sit outside the top 130 on ESPN.
Experts call him a useful late-round center and a value pick around round 8 in 10-team mock drafts, mostly for his defensive stats.
OKC is projected to win about 62 games and to be a top two seed in the West.

durable.text: He is an unusual center who gets assists and no longer shoots threes. He adds rebounds, steals, blocks and a high FG%.
He is a very low scorer. He does not fit every fantasy team, but he can help plenty of them.

note: Hartenstein is a late-auction center: Yahoo values him at 5 USD and ESPN at 0 USD, with average costs around 1 USD. Our league paid 11 USD for him last season, which is too much for a rank near 104 to 132. He fits punt 3PM builds and teams that need rebounds, FG% and assists from the center spot, and he costs little in turnovers. Early in the season, check his ankle (Yahoo Q) and whether he gets the 28 or more minutes that experts say would make him a top 60 player.
